description: Flag-round amendment voting scenarios. One round is one flag ledger; close time advances flag_interval_s per round. Majority must be held for majority_time_s (two weeks) from the round the majority is first recorded. Votes are counts of trusted validators voting yes; trusted is the UNL size unless an event changes it. The simulator implements AmendmentSet threshold math (integer division, pre-fix >=, post-fix strict > with the single-validator >= exception), TrustedVotes 24h expiry as scheduled vote drops, the validator-quorum gate, and the doVoting branch order (GotMajority / LostMajority / Enable / Hold). A scenario may contain several runs (A, B, ...) that share the scenario parameters but differ in their event schedule.

scenarios.description: Pre-fix boundary at UNL 35: threshold is (35*204)//256 = 27, and 27 yes votes pass with >=. Run B with 26 votes fails to gain majority. Tests the exact pre-fix boundary.
scenarios.title: Pre-fix boundary: 27 of 35 passes

scenarios.description: Post-fix boundary at UNL 35: threshold is (35*67)//100 = 23, and the strict > rule needs 24 yes votes. Run B with 23 votes fails. Tests the exact post-fix boundary.
scenarios.title: Post-fix boundary: 24 of 35 passes, 23 fails

scenarios.description: Post-fix minority veto at UNL 35: 24 yes / 11 no passes, while 23 yes / 12 no fails. A 12-validator minority (34.3%) blocks the amendment.
scenarios.title: Minority veto: 12 of 35 no-voters block (post-fix)

scenarios.description: Support 30 of 35 for 960 rounds (~10 days), one round at 20, then 30 again. The single dip emits tfLostMajority and restarts the two-week clock from the re-gain round; enablement is delayed by 961 rounds versus the no-dip case.
scenarios.title: One-round dip below threshold restarts the clock

scenarios.description: Support 30 of 35 for 480 rounds, then 15 forever. Majority is gained, then lost at round 480; the amendment never enables.
scenarios.title: Support gained then lost permanently

scenarios.description: UNL churn that survives: at round 500 five validators leave (UNL 35 -> 30, yes votes 30 -> 25). Threshold recomputes from 23 to 20; 25 > 20 still passes and the amendment enables on the original schedule.
scenarios.title: Validator churn that keeps the majority

scenarios.description: UNL churn that kills the majority: at round 500 six yes-voters leave (UNL 35 -> 29, yes votes 24 -> 18). Threshold recomputes to 19; 18 is not > 19, so tfLostMajority fires and the amendment never enables.
scenarios.title: Validator churn that kills the majority

scenarios.description: Single trusted validator: threshold is max(1, 67//100) = 1 and the single-validator exception uses >=, so 1 vote passes even under the post-fix strict-> rule. Enables on schedule.
scenarios.title: Single-validator network passes on one vote

scenarios.description: Small UNL 5 regime flip. Pre-fix threshold is (5*204)//256 = 3 and 3 votes pass with >= (60%). Post-fix threshold is (5*67)//100 = 3 but the strict > rule needs 4 votes (80%). Same vote count, opposite outcome across regimes.
scenarios.title: Small UNL 5: 3 votes pass pre-fix, fail post-fix

scenarios.description: TrustedVotes 24-hour expiry. Pre-fix UNL 35 with 28 yes votes: one validator goes silent and its vote expires at round 97 (votes 27, still >= 27); a second expires at round 120 (votes 26, majority lost); both return at round 200 (votes 28) and the clock restarts from round 200.
scenarios.title: 24-hour vote expiry delays then restarts the hold

scenarios.description: Support drops below threshold in the exact round the two-week hold completes (round 1344). doVoting checks the lost-majority branch before the enable branch, so only tfLostMajority is emitted and the amendment is NOT enabled. The xrpl.org note says the amendment is ultimately enabled in this case; the code path modelled here says otherwise. Divergence case.
scenarios.title: Support lost in the exact round the hold completes

scenarios.description: Local veto only. The local node vetoes (local_vote_up false) so it never proposes the enable transaction, but 30 of 35 validators support the amendment and non-vetoing nodes propose enablement. The amendment enables on schedule at round 1344 despite the local veto.
scenarios.title: Local veto does not block network enablement

scenarios.description: Validator-quorum gate. UNL 35 has quorum max(ceil(35*0.67), ceil(35*0.6)) = 24. Run A with only 23 trusted validations present skips amendment voting entirely even though 30 of the 35 validators vote yes. Run B with 24 present proceeds and the amendment gains majority.
scenarios.title: Quorum gate: 23 validations skip voting, 24 proceed
